title: In-place high-three-byte buffer packing
summary: Recovered VA 0x55d1c0 as a member method: retain bytes 1,2,3 of each complete four-byte group in order, compact in place, and replace the uint32 size at +8 with the bytes written. Data pointer +0 and unknown field +4 remain unchanged. Direct callers at 0x55d235 and 0x55d296 use a subobject at +0x6cd8 of the surrounding format-conversion object.
test_description: GCC i386 thiscall oracle comparison for all lengths 0..1027 and 4093..4100, varying byte patterns and alignment, two consecutive conversions, null buffers for sizes 0..3. Independently check packed bytes and length, all buffer bytes including discarded tail and external guards, data pointer and unknown field. Install test FS backing and check head after every oracle call.
known_limits: Original semantic class name, +4 field meaning, and caller format names are unresolved.
Valid writable backing is required; invalid pointers, buffers overlapping the object, and fault behavior are not modeled or tested.
Near-UINT32_MAX lengths can wrap the original next-group check and overrun backing; unsigned check arithmetic is retained but these invalid-size executions are untested.
No byte-identical code generation claim; return-register residue is not modeled as a return value.
